title: Zephyr identity store lacks authenticated rollback authority
description: The versioned lichen/identity Settings record added by l1qw.11.2.1 detects accidental corruption with CRC and prevents ordinary API replacement, but it has no device-secret MAC or independent monotonic/deletion anchor. An offline stale/forged record+marker can therefore become authoritative, and future key rotation cannot reject an older valid identity. Add an injected protected rollback-authority contract (HUK/secure-element/monotonic protected storage supplied by platform), authenticate and bind format/EUI/seed/pubkey/revision, require exact record+anchor agreement, fail closed on one-sided deletion/rollback/divergence, and add deterministic corruption/forgery/rollback/torn/reboot tests without requiring physical hardware validation.
notes: Implemented protected rollback-authority injection for identity persistence. Format v2 binds magic/version/reserved bytes, monotonic u64 revision, EUI-64, seed, derived pubkey, and CRC into a BLAKE2b-256 digest anchored outside ordinary Settings. Restore requires exact record+marker+authority revision/digest agreement; virgin state is authorized only when authority and both Settings blobs are absent. One-sided deletion, stale revision, forged/divergent digest, corrupt/torn/unavailable state all fail closed. First boot saves record+marker, then atomically commits the protected authority before publishing the key. Settings convenience APIs now require a one-time platform authority registration and otherwise return -EACCES. Added isolated qemu_x86 harness so validation does not link the actively changing unrelated Link library. Validation: Zephyr 4.1 qemu_x86 build warning-free; runtime 13/13 PASS, PROJECT EXECUTION SUCCESSFUL. The ordinary app_identity QEMU build also compiled identity_store.c, identity_settings.c, and test objects before stopping at unrelated live identity_addr.c crypto_sha512 collision; no collided file was touched.
